body:
1.3.8 is it actually a requirement for injection section?

* V1.3.8 Verify that the application escapes special characters in regular expressions (typically using a backslash) to prevent them from being misinterpreted as metacharacters.

Based on #1600 the category choice seemed like a temporary choice with one option to put it into "code review".

If there are no good arguments why it must stay in sanitization, I propose to move into "V1.2 Injection Prevention"

comments.body:
I think V1.3.8 implies user data being used inside of a RegEx itself. This would basically be RegEx injection which will let me bypass validation and perform RegExDos which I think is covered elsewhere.

Even better, don't let user data drive RegEx's at all.

But I think that is what the intention of this was long ago.

I'd think the goal here is to prevent RegEx injections (not RegEx DoS).

> and perform RegExDos which I think is covered elsewhere.

There might be legitimate use cases for user-chosen RegEx. For example,

* an application which supports validation of user-chosen JSON Schema (which [includes RegEx](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/regular_expressions)).

This should still be allowed but the risk on RegEx DoS should be mitigated in this case.

For regex dos we have:
> V1.3.13 Verify that regular expressions are free from elements causing exponential backtracking, and ensure untrusted input is sanitized to mitigate ReDoS or Runaway Regex attacks.
